qualifying_findings.title: pg-aiguide MCP HTTP transport accepted arbitrary Host headers
qualifying_findings.summary: NVD records that pg-aiguide started its MCP HTTP transport without enabling the SDK host allow-list, allowing DNS rebinding through a browser-controlled hostname to drive a locally reachable MCP server. Version 0.5.1 explicitly passes the protection option.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public vulnerability database entry with vendor repository and patch pull request references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: pg-aiguide through 0.5.0; fixed in 0.5.1 according to NVD description.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A local MCP server can become an unauthorized tool-control endpoint when browser-origin traffic can bypass host-header protections, collapsing the boundary between web content and local AI tool authority.

upstream_routing.reason: pg-aiguide as a product/MCP server is upstream-owned; this repository should retain only the MCP DNS-rebinding and host-allow-list security implication.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence in the technical fact from NVD and VulnCheck references; publication predates the 48-hour cutoff, but NVD exposes an exact in-window lastModified timestamp.

qualifying_findings.title: tiger-gh-mcp-server exposed a browser-drivable GitHub MCP endpoint
qualifying_findings.summary: NVD records that tiger-gh-mcp-server started its MCP HTTP transport without the SDK DNS-rebinding host allow-list, allowing a browser page to drive the locally reachable GitHub MCP endpoint through an attacker-controlled hostname. The fix passes the option explicitly alongside a dependency update.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public vulnerability database entry with vendor repository and patch pull request references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Commit boundary before the fix; no release bracket was published according to NVD.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: GitHub-scoped MCP tools often carry repository authority, so local transport host validation is a least-privilege and delegated-authority control, not just a network hardening detail.

upstream_routing.reason: The MCP server entity belongs upstream; local retention should focus on MCP transport host validation and delegated GitHub authority.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence in the technical fact from NVD and VulnCheck references; publication predates the 48-hour cutoff, but NVD exposes an exact in-window lastModified timestamp.

qualifying_findings.title: Skyvern TextPromptBlock double-rendering enabled Jinja sandbox escape
qualifying_findings.summary: Skyvern before 1.0.45 rendered TextPromptBlock prompts first through a sandboxed Jinja environment and then through an unsandboxed environment. Attackers could inject Jinja template syntax through workflow parameters or upstream block output to execute code with server process privileges.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public vulnerability database entry with primary advisory and patch commit references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Skyvern >= 0.2.1 and < 1.0.45 according to VulnCheck; NVD records Skyvern before 1.0.45.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: It turns prompt or workflow data into server-side code execution in a browser automation agent platform, making prompt handling and template rendering part of the execution sandbox boundary.

upstream_routing.reason: Skyvern as an AI browser automation product is upstream-owned; the prompt-template sandbox escape and workflow-boundary implication are local security material.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: NVD, VulnCheck, repository, and patch commit are public and align on the affected boundary.

qualifying_findings.title: browser-use web-ui accepted arbitrary recording and trace paths
qualifying_findings.summary: browser-use web-ui 2.0.0 through 3.0.0 failed to validate browser settings paths in run_agent_task. Attackers could supply absolute paths for recording, trace, history, or download locations through the unauthenticated Gradio interface and create directories where the root-running container had write access.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public vulnerability database entry with primary advisory and GitHub issue references
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent browsers produce recordings, traces, histories, and downloads; path controls are part of containment for autonomous browser runtimes and their forensic artifacts.

upstream_routing.reason: Browser Use product context belongs upstream; this repository keeps the browser-agent path containment failure and artifact-boundary implication.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from NVD and VulnCheck; patched version was not confirmed in the fetched public sources.

qualifying_findings.title: jina-ai Reader disabled private-address SSRF guard outside Google Cloud
qualifying_findings.summary: jina-ai Reader disabled its private-address guard outside Google Cloud deployments, allowing unauthenticated SSRF by supplying public hostnames that resolved to private addresses and could retrieve cloud metadata or internal service content.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public vulnerability database entry with primary advisory and GitHub issue references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: NVD did not expose a version range in the fetched summary; issue and advisory references need ingest-time patch-boundary reconciliation.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Reader-style web retrieval services often feed model context; SSRF can turn retrieval into internal network and cloud metadata exposure, contaminating both data security and prompt-context trust boundaries.

upstream_routing.reason: Jina Reader as a product/entity belongs upstream; SSRF, metadata exposure, and retrieval-boundary analysis belong locally.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence in the vulnerability fact; affected-version and remediation details require follow-up during ingest.

qualifying_findings.title: NextChat proxy URL validation exposed OpenAI API keys
qualifying_findings.summary: NextChat 2.15.8 through 2.16.1 used substring matching for the x-base-url proxy header instead of hostname parsing. An attacker could use any URL containing api.openai.com and receive the server's OpenAI API key in the Authorization header.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public vulnerability database entry with primary advisory and GitHub issue references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: NextChat versions 2.15.8 through 2.16.1 according to NVD; VulnCheck lists NextChat <= 2.16.1.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Provider API keys are delegated model authority and spend authority; proxy URL validation errors can move them to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

upstream_routing.reason: NextChat and OpenAI provider background belong upstream; this repo keeps the API-key disclosure and proxy-host validation control implication.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from NVD and VulnCheck; ingestion should reconcile whether the inclusive lower bound differs between NVD and VulnCheck.

qualifying_findings.title: browser-use web-ui stored configured LLM API keys in cleartext
qualifying_findings.summary: browser-use web-ui 2.0.0 through 3.0.0 wrote configured LLM API keys to predictably named JSON files without encryption or access restrictions, allowing attackers with local read access to the temporary settings directory to recover provider keys.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public vulnerability database entry with primary advisory and GitHub issue references
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Browser agents often hold provider credentials for autonomous action; local secret storage decisions determine whether a compromised runtime or adjacent user can take over model/provider authority.

upstream_routing.reason: Browser Use product context belongs upstream; secret storage and provider-key authority boundaries are local security material.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from NVD and VulnCheck; patched version was not confirmed in the fetched public sources.

qualifying_findings.title: Keploy exposed unauthenticated agent control-plane TLS key logs
qualifying_findings.summary: Keploy 3.1.0 through 3.6.25 bound its agent control-plane HTTP server to all interfaces without authentication. Attackers could access /agent/pcap/keylog for NSS keylog lines to decrypt recorded TLS traffic, or invoke /agent/stop and /agent/storemocks to manipulate recording sessions.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public vulnerability database entry with primary advisory, GitHub issue, and patch commit references
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI-assisted testing and replay tools can capture sensitive traffic; unauthenticated agent control planes expose test evidence, credentials in transit, and recording integrity.

upstream_routing.reason: Keploy as a general development/testing workflow tool routes to ai-dev-wiki; this repository keeps the security-control-plane and captured-traffic exposure implication.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from NVD, VulnCheck, issue, and patch commit references.
